testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Why are roads slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when it first rains. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road surface, creating a slippery layer. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: What can improperly loaded cargo do?

options.text: Look bad to others on the road.
Injure the driver during a quick stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Injure the driver during a quick stop.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded and secured properly. During a quick stop, loose cargo can shift or fall and hurt or even kill the driver.

questions.question: Where are ABS malfunction lamps on trucks and buses?

options.text: On the outside near the passenger door

questions.explanation: Trucks and buses with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lamps on their instrument panels. Trailers have yellow ABS lamps on their left side, at the front or back corner.

questions.question: During an inspection, brake pads should be:
questions.explanation: When inspecting brakes, make sure the pads have no oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If the truck has open space.
If hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of material is being carried and warn others of dangers.

questions.question: When exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.

questions.explanation: When exiting during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and always keep three points of contact. For a bus, hold the handrail firmly. Exiting incorrectly results in automatic failure.

questions.question: Which is NOT a distracted person drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in the vehicle
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to others may not pay attention to the road. Children may run into traffic without looking. Be careful near road workers. A person waiting on a bench is not a traffic concern.

questions.question: Which may cause someone to be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: They are not a lawful permanent U.S. resident.
They were convicted of speeding in the last three years.
They answered some questions wrong on the hazmat test.
They did not pass the hazmat test on their first try.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not a lawful permanent U.S. resident.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazmat endorsement if you are not a lawful U.S. permanent resident, renounce citizenship, are wanted or convicted of certain crimes, are judged mentally unfit, or are considered a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: Who is responsible for inspecting a vehicle's cargo?
questions.explanation: The driver must inspect the cargo. They must check for overloading, poor weight balance, proper securing, and that cargo does not block their view or emergency equipment. Drivers are always responsible for their cargo.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, you should:

options.text: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you near the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid a hazard, keep both hands on the steering wheel. You need a firm grip to turn quickly and safely.

questions.question: A CMV must have:

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Use turn signals only when another vehicle is next to you.
Not use a turn signal if your lane change is obvious.
Always use turn signals to tell others your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others your plans.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The nuts need to be replaced.
The nuts are the wrong size.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts means they are loose. Check and tighten them if you see rust.

questions.question: Texting while driving a CMV is:

options.text: Okay if the text is about work.
Okay if the message has fewer than 10 words.
Safer than talking on the phone.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is illegal and dangerous. This includes typing or reading any text on an electronic device.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of a highway, where should you place warning devices behind your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your stopped CMV on a highway.

questions.question: You should always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop completely within the area of road you can see in front of you.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include all of the following except:
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include: trip dates, start and end points, route, starting and ending odometer readings, total distance, distance traveled in-jurisdiction, and vehicle number.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a problem if passengers are not getting off.
Should not be on the road.

questions.explanation: Always be careful around stopped buses. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus, and the bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving a CMV:

options.text: You don't need to wear a safety belt.
You only need a safety belt if your vehicle has no airbags.
You only need a safety belt if carrying more than 1,000 pounds.
You must always wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection in a crash. You must always wear a safety belt when driving a CMV.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is clear ice that lets you see the road surface through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be very careful when it's freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What is the safe maximum amount of play on a 20-inch steering wheel?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts unique to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three braking systems: service, parking, and emergency. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle, what should you check for?

options.text: The vehicle is shiner than others.
The vehicle is not parked too closely to other vehicles.
There are not puddles under the vehicle that indicate a leak.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are not puddles under the vehicle that indicate a leak.
questions.explanation: When approaching your vehicle, check its general condition and look for damage. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Also check for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how should you brake?

options.text: Stop harder than you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make the ABS activate.
Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When inspecting cargo, which is NOT required?

options.text: That the truck is not overloaded.
That the cargo is secured properly.
That the cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the cargo is heavier at the top than the bottom.
questions.explanation: When inspecting cargo, ensure it is balanced and properly secured. Keep weight as low as possible to prevent rollovers. Do not overload the trailer.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you when you need to brake?

options.text: Tap on the brakes a couple of times.
Stick your arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap on the brakes a couple of times.
questions.explanation: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.

questions.question: After changing a tire, why should you stop after a short distance?

options.text: Check the tightness of the lug nuts.
Ensure that the tire tread depth is good.
Ensure that the correct tire was changed.
See if rocks have gotten into the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the tightness of the lug nuts.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop shortly after to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: If a tire fails, what should you do?

options.text: Loosen your grip on the steering wheel.
Check your tires after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your tires after coming to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the steering wheel firmly. Do not use the brakes. Let the vehicle slow down on its own. When it has slowed, brake gently, pull off the road, and stop. Then check your tires.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which shows poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks.
Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available.
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when more than one lane is available.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, and stop signs. Complete turns in the proper lane. Use or stay in the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving, what should you do?

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
Check the lights from inside the vehicle.
Check the lights by looking at a reflection in a shiny surface.

questions.explanation: To check your vehicle's lights, turn off the engine and remove the key. Set the parking brake. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle and look at the lights to make sure they work.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under it.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle has enough room to pass under an overhead object, slow down. Find another route if you can.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, what is most important?

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses have no fluid in them.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Look for leaks and fix them before driving.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, what must you do?
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: How should you handle a burning tire?

options.text: Cut it up with an axe.

questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need to use a large amount of water.

questions.question: While driving, spring brakes are held in place by what?
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure gets too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: Before winter driving, what should you check?
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heating and defrosting equipment, coolant and antifreeze levels, wipers and washers, tire tread, tire chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Clear ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, hand holds, steps, and deck plates.

questions.question: What is the legal blood alcohol limit for operating a CMV?
questions.explanation: Operating a CMV with a blood alcohol level of 0.04 percent or higher is illegal. A first offense results in losing your license for at least one year. Any detectable alcohol below 0.04 percent results in being put out-of-service for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts.
questions.explanation: When checking the exhaust system, look for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, and brackets. Check for leaks and for parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts. Parts NOT rubbing against other parts is normal and not a concern.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Stop the front tires from overheating.
Use brakes equally on all wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Front brake limiting valves were designed to reduce the risk of front wheel skidding. However, research shows they are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: What is the most common type of foundation brake?
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: What do federal and state laws require drivers to do?

options.text: Inspect their vehicles only if they suspect a problem
Inspect their vehicles only when traveling out-of-state
Inspect their vehicles only when transporting hazardous materials

questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require commercial drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help identify problems before they become dangerous or expensive.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal activate?

options.text: When tank pressure falls below 120 psi
When tank pressure falls below 60 psi
When tank pressure falls below 10 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure falls below 60 psi
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning signal must activate when air tank pressure falls below 60 psi. This warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: How can you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot from the brake pedal
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward
Fully engage the clutch before lifting your foot from the brake pedal
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot from the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before lifting your foot from the brake to prevent rolling backward. Use the parking brake whenever needed to keep the vehicle from rolling back.

questions.question: How many licenses can a driver have?

options.text: Two—one for automobiles and one for trucks
One for each state where they plan to drive
An automobile license from one state and a CDL from another

questions.explanation: A person can have only one license. States share driver information through a computer database to prevent duplicate licenses.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: A warm, poorly-ventilated cab makes you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or turn on the air conditioning to keep the cab cool and reduce fatigue.

questions.question: How soon must you place emergency warning devices after stopping on the side of the road?
questions.explanation: Place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the shoulder. Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when pulling off the road.

questions.question: What is a sign that a driver is distracted?

options.text: Not talking to anyone in the vehicle

questions.explanation: Signs of distracted driving include drifting within lanes, changing speeds, using a cell phone, looking at maps or food, or talking to passengers.

questions.question: What should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the daytime.

questions.question: What should you do first when backing your vehicle into an alley?

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space
Turn your vehicle right to position it directly in front of the alley
Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the alley. Your vehicle should be parked straight within the parking space boundaries.
